25.explanation: Not every Ramsar site is notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Ramsar sites can overlap national parks or sanctuaries. Ramsar listing creates treaty obligations but does not by itself give legal protection enforceable against the State.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal) becomes India's 100th Ramsar Site

26.note: Surha Tal is an oxbow lake of the Ganga (Ballia); Ganga is not among the options. Ghaghara also flows through Ballia district—confirm intended answer.

27.explanation: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites where ecological change has happened, is happening or is likely.

28.explanation: Sasthamkotta Lake is in Kerala (Kollam), not Tamil Nadu. The other pairs are correct.

29.explanation: All three apply: Ramsar protects wetland habitat, the CBD covers biodiversity broadly, and the CMS deals with migratory species (including the Central Asian Flyway).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species

30.explanation: Tamil Nadu, not Uttar Pradesh, has the most Ramsar sites. The other statements are true: Ramsar 1971; Chilika and Keoladeo first designated in 1981; JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal, UP) is the 100th site.

sources.title: Onmanorama: JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary becomes 100th Ramsar site (13th in UP)

31.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equal opportunity in public employment and bars discrimination on grounds including sex.

32.explanation: Bihar has given female government employees two days of menstrual leave a month since 1992.

33.explanation: Since the 2017 amendment, a woman with fewer than two surviving children gets up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave.

34.explanation: Under a continuing mandamus the Supreme Court keeps a case open and monitors compliance over time.

sources.title: Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1998)

35.explanation: Separation of powers stops courts from doing the legislature's or executive's core policy work, such as framing leave policy.

36.explanation: Trade unions, industrial disputes and labour welfare are in the Concurrent List (Entries 22–24, List III).

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule List III

37.explanation: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 raised the threshold for prior permission for layoff, retrenchment or closure from 100 to 300 workers.

38.explanation: Striking is not a fundamental right (All India Bank Employees' Assn., 1962; T.K. Rangarajan, 2003). The Trade Unions Act, 1926 gave strikes limited recognition through immunities. India is a founding member of the ILO (1919).

sources.title: T.K. Rangarajan v. Govt of Tamil Nadu (2003)

39.explanation: Under s.2(l) of the ID Act a lockout is an employer closing the workplace or suspending work.

40.explanation: The Code on Social Security, 2020 recognises gig and platform workers for welfare schemes but does not treat them as employees with full labour rights.

41.explanation: The four codes cover Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions. There is no Vocational Training code.

43.explanation: Double deflation deflates outputs and inputs with separate price indices to get real GVA.

44.explanation: ASUSE is NSO's Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises.

45.explanation: The Provisional Estimates (May 2026) put FY2025–26 real GDP growth at about 7.7% on the new 2022–23 base, later revised to 7.8% in NAS 2026.

49.explanation: Pithoragarh district and the road to Lipulekh are in Uttarakhand.

50.explanation: Accretion is a gradual, natural shift of a river's course, which moves the boundary with it. Avulsion is a sudden shift, which leaves the boundary where it was.
